stories.head: 60%+ of consumers start shopping with AI tools — your data is now your brand
stories.plain: Gary Lombardo of Athos Commerce argues that when the majority of shoppers begin their journey inside an AI discovery engine, traditional top-of-funnel marketing is bypassed entirely. The new imperative: structured, high-quality first-party data that AI systems can surface. This reframes what 'brand' means and changes how marketers should invest.

stories.head: Airship achieves ISO 42001 AI governance certification, first mover in CX industry
stories.plain: Airship is among the first customer engagement platforms to earn the global ISO 42001 AI management standard. This matters because enterprise buyers increasingly require governance credentials before procurement, and EU AI Act readiness is becoming a hard buying criterion. It shifts governance from a soft talking point to a contractual requirement.

stories.head: Your AI visibility score may be hiding a problem: brand mentions vs. source citations diverge
stories.plain: Marketers tracking AI visibility often conflate two very different signals: being mentioned by an AI answer versus being cited as a source. Each requires a different fix, and confusing them wastes budget. This practical diagnostic reframes how teams should measure and act on their generative engine presence.

stories.head: Druid AI adds governance, auditability, and agent interoperability to move AI from pilot to production
stories.plain: Druid AI released platform updates covering voice interfaces, cross-agent interoperability, and built-in governance and evaluation tools designed to get agentic AI out of sandboxes and into live enterprise workflows. For buyers, this signals that auditability is now a product feature, not an afterthought — changing what enterprise AI procurement checklists look like.

stories.head: MNTN integrates Tealium CDP audiences into AI-powered Connected TV targeting
stories.plain: MNTN's native Tealium integration lets advertisers push first-party CDP audiences directly into CTV campaign targeting, combining verified customer data with AI household matching. As third-party signals erode, this shows how CDPs are becoming the essential upstream data source for performance advertising across emerging channels like streaming TV.

stories.head: Expert Mode: 60%+ of consumers start shopping in AI tools — your data is your new brand
stories.plain: When most shoppers begin their journey inside an AI assistant, brands lose control of the funnel's top. Gary Lombardo argues that first-party data is now the primary brand asset — not creative or media spend. This reframes how marketers should think about data strategy, GEO, and what 'discovery' even means in 2026.

stories.head: Airship achieves ISO 42001 certification, advancing EU AI Act readiness for CX platforms
stories.plain: Airship is among the first customer engagement platforms to earn ISO 42001 — the global AI management systems standard. This matters because enterprise procurement teams and EU AI Act compliance officers are starting to require it. It signals that governance certification is becoming a real buying criterion, not just a checkbox.

stories.head: Survey of 47 B2B agencies reveals how GEO is being priced, packaged and sold
stories.plain: The first substantive agency-side look at how Generative Engine Optimization is being commercialized: what agencies charge, how they scope the work, and what enterprise buyers should expect. Useful because it moves GEO from concept to actual market practice, giving buyers a benchmark for evaluating vendors.

stories.head: Your AI visibility score may be hiding a problem: brand mentions vs. source citations tell different stories
stories.plain: Being mentioned in an AI answer and being cited as a trusted source are two very different signals — and many marketers are tracking only one. Conflating brand mentions with authoritative citations leads to wrong fixes. This piece gives practitioners a clearer diagnostic framework for AI-search presence.

stories.head: Druid AI adds governance and auditability to move enterprise agents from pilot to production
stories.plain: Druid AI's new release targets the #1 blocker of enterprise AI deployment: lack of governance and auditability. New capabilities cover agent interoperability, voice, and evaluation tools designed to satisfy IT and legal review boards. This is a concrete product signal that governed agentic AI is moving from aspiration to shippable feature.

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Customer Interface
body: Autonomous AI agents are no longer a future concept — they are actively inserting themselves between brands and buyers, filtering decisions, summarising offers, and reducing direct human touchpoints. Seismic pushing agentic revenue execution into every GTM workflow, and Druid AI adding agent interoperability & governance, show how quickly the stack is being re-plumbed around agent-to-agent handoffs.

The strategic consequence is stark: marketers who optimise for human eyes risk becoming invisible to the agents that now pre-select options for real buyers. Teams must plan for both human and machine audiences simultaneously, or cede the top of funnel to whoever's agents are better trained.

themes.head: First-Party Data as the New Brand Asset
body: As channels fragment and third-party signals erode, proprietary customer data is becoming a durable competitive moat — not just a targeting input. MNTN pulling Tealium first-party data directly into AI-powered TV targeting, and ZoomInfo folding Workbounce's enterprise knowledge into its GTM context graph, both illustrate that the race is now about who owns the richest, most connected data layer.

Gary Lombardo's framing — 'your data is your new brand' — captures the shift cleanly: media budgets rent attention, but a well-structured first-party graph compounds over time. Organisations that treat data infrastructure as a cost centre rather than a brand investment are likely to find themselves outmanoeuvred by leaner rivals with better-connected signals.

themes.head: Generative Engine Optimisation — Beyond Traditional SEO
body: Google's updated content guidance and the rise of AI-generated answer surfaces have rendered classic SEO metrics misleading. MarTech's warning that 'your AI visibility score may be hiding a problem' underscores that brands can appear to rank well in legacy dashboards while quietly disappearing from the LLM-driven answers that increasingly shape buyer awareness.

Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) demands a fundamentally different content strategy: structured, citable, authoritative content that AI systems can confidently surface and attribute. This is not an incremental update to existing SEO playbooks — it is a new discipline requiring new measurement frameworks and new editorial standards.

themes.head: AI Governance & Trust Becoming Table Stakes
body: Regulatory pressure and buyer scepticism are forcing AI deployments out of the 'move fast' phase into a governed, auditable one. Airship achieving ISO 42001 certification, Sitecore expanding sovereign cloud hosting for its AI into regulated markets, and PropellerAds flagging malware guardrails for agentic media buying all signal that governance is no longer a legal afterthought — it is a sales prerequisite.

The 'people still trust people over pixels' finding reinforces why: enterprise buyers and consumers alike are applying a trust discount to AI-generated experiences. Vendors that can demonstrate certified, transparent AI processes are gaining a procurement edge, particularly in financial services, healthcare, and public-sector verticals where compliance is non-negotiable.

themes.head: The CMO Role & Marketing Org Under Structural Pressure
body: AI is not just changing what marketing does — it is exposing a mismatch between what modern marketing requires and how most organisations are structured to support it. MarTech's analysis that 'marketing has outgrown the organisation built to run it' resonates alongside the Q4 2026 state-of-AI report showing AI budgets growing faster than proof of ROI, creating accountability gaps at the executive level.

The CMO's remit is simultaneously expanding (owning data strategy, AI governance, revenue attribution) and being challenged from below by MOps teams restructuring around autonomous agents. The practical upshot: organisations need clearer role definitions — not everyone should be an AI builder — and CMOs must make the case for measurement frameworks before budgets outrun evidence of impact.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — data, agents, search, governance, and org design — the common thread is that AI is forcing decisions that were previously deferrable, and the brands that move from experimentation to structured commitment now will set the defaults everyone else inherits.
